title: INI parser
prompt:
We can write config files with stringifyIni() in src/ini.js but we still read them with a regex hack in each service. Please add an exported parseIni(text) to src/ini.js that implements the dialect described in docs/INI_FORMAT.md.

It returns a plain object of sections, each a plain object of string values, e.g. parseIni("[server]\nport = 8080\n") gives { server: { port: "8080" } }. Please follow the doc exactly, in particular: full-line comments only, keys before the first header go in the "" section, duplicate sections merge (last value wins for a repeated key), quoted values with the four escapes, backslash line continuation, and both \n and \r\n line endings.

Bad input must throw a SyntaxError with a numeric line property (1-based) pointing at the offending line, as the doc describes; the message wording is up to you. parseIni(stringifyIni(data)) should give back data for string values.
acceptance: Sections and trimming, the "" section and its omission, full-line comments only, literal section names and empty sections, split on first '=', merged duplicate sections with last-wins keys and first-appearance order, quoted values and escapes, continuation joining, CRLF, round trip with stringifyIni, SyntaxError with the right line for every listed error including continuation at end of file.
difficulty_rationale: One parser but many interacting edge cases (quoting, escapes, continuation, merging, error line numbers) spelled out in a format doc.
